builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: CompAct-Bench: A Benchmark for Working-Context Compaction in Long-Horizon Agent Tasks
summary: CompAct-Bench evaluates LLM-based working-context compaction as a replacement for unbounded history accumulation in long-horizon agents, using controlled retention ratios across BrowseComp, SWE-bench, and an internal CompanyBench. Adopting compaction costs quality rather than infrastructure: even frontier models degrade downstream task accuracy under aggressive compression, and the iterative ratio-adjustment evaluation itself requires extra inference passes. After adoption, failures arise from distorted task state—unresolved issues rendered as conclusions and forgotten established results—causing incorrect decisions and redundant execution rather than mere information loss.
rationale: The paper is an evaluation benchmark, not an adoptable method, so the actionable takeaway is the documented failure modes of LLM-based compaction rather than a technique to deploy.
technique: Benchmark of working-context compaction for agents

claims.statement: CompAct-Bench evaluates LLM-based working-context compaction as a replacement for unbounded history accumulation in long-horizon agents, using controlled retention ratios across BrowseComp, SWE-bench, and an internal CompanyBench. Adopting compaction costs quality rather than infrastructure: even frontier models degrade downstream task accuracy under aggressive compression, and the iterative ratio-adjustment evaluation itself requires extra inference passes. After adoption, failures arise from distorted task state—unresolved issues rendered as conclusions and forgotten established results—causing incorrect decisions and redundant execution rather than mere information loss.

Frontier Claude- and GPT-family compactors perform strongest overall, but substantial degradation in downstream task accuracy persists under aggressive compaction; no multiplicative improvement factor is reported.
